extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, journal editors, and researchers who write or study peer-review reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for writing high-quality peer-review reports for academic journals, covering what to tell authors and editors, tone, structure, and specific manuscript-assessment criteria across sections and methodological aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments to the author
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback intended for the authors aimed at offering recommendations for manuscript improvement; should emphasize strengths and point out shortcomings that can be addressed during revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary objective is to offer recommendations and be supportive even when recommending rejection. Comments to authors should clarify the reviewer’s decision but should not include the publication recommendation (which should be confidential). Align comments to authors with comments to the editor (content should be consistent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments to the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential remarks placed in a separate section for the editor, summarizing assessment and justifying the recommendation (accept, reject, revise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be concise but offer objective assessment supported by clear reasoning and additional information to help editorial decision-making; should not merely repeat what is conveyed to authors but provide rationale based on quality and relevance of the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Language and manner used in the review should be fair, balanced, polite, and civil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use professional, non-accusatory language that does not belittle authors; be collegial and constructive; reviewers should be courteous and respectful, giving constructive criticism kindly. Downplay excessive praise; maintain ability to identify significant flaws without being harsh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and organization of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Review should be clear, concise, and organized to help authors and editors interpret and act on feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a brief overview of main strengths and weaknesses; structure comments according to manuscript sections (abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion); prioritize and distinguish major vs minor issues; number points and, if appropriate, divide into major and minor criticisms to facilitate responses and editorial evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive/helpful
rubrics_metrics.description: Review should provide actionable suggestions that help authors improve the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer recommendations that guide revision (not just criticism). Even in rejection, give guidance for improvement or future submission. Avoid 'hijacking' the work (e.g., suggesting irrelevant references or unnecessary rewrites).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should be concrete and precise rather than vague or overly general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific examples, point to exact sections/lines, explain why something is problematic, and suggest precise remedies rather than offering only general statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Review should be impartial, avoiding personal biases and undue influence of reviewer preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the manuscript’s merits and methodological rigor rather than reviewer idiosyncratic tastes; disclose conflicts of interest; be mindful of fairness in recommendations such as rejection vs revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness / comprehensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Review should address the manuscript in sufficient depth to evaluate its scientific quality and trustworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover essential components of the paper (structure, approach, ethics, scientific value); avoid overly brief feedback that lacks actionable suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability / organization / clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Review text should itself be readable, well-organized and clearly communicate key points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use logical ordering, brief overviews, numbered points, and section-based organization to make the review easy to follow for authors and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a professional and civil manner throughout the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid demeaning or negative language; criticism should be delivered respectfully to foster productive dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Base assessments on evidence and reasoning rather than personal opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support judgments with clear rationale, refer to methods/data/textual evidence, and avoid conjecture or speculation not grounded in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure internal consistency within the review and alignment between comments to authors and comments to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not give contradictory messages in different sections; ensure that the substance of comments to authors is reflected (appropriately) in the confidential editor comments, while not revealing editorial recommendation to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a quality review
rubrics_metrics.description: A quality review is represented by features such as constructiveness, specificity, fairness, thoroughness, readability, professional tone, objectivity, and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality reviews go beyond standard checklist criteria and meet the eight identified quality features; they avoid subjectivity by following objective requirements for content and report writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of publication recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation on publication (accept/reject/revise) should generally be communicated only to the editor, not to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most studies advise keeping publication recommendation confidential; however, some disagreement exists in the literature. Default guidance: share recommendation with editor only and provide clear justifications in confidential comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar and language scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether reviewers should correct grammar and language vs focusing solely on scientific content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is inconsistency: some guidelines ask reviewers to address grammar/style/spelling/punctuation; others argue language correction is copy-editor responsibility and reviewers should prioritize content and scientific merit. Use judgment and journal-specific norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback when rejecting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide constructive feedback even when recommending rejection, tailored to the reasons for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejection is for fixable issues, give guidance for improvement; if for fundamental design flaws, prioritize major methodological criticisms over minor issues like grammar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding reviewer self-promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use review to unduly promote the reviewer’s own work or irrelevant references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid suggesting irrelevant references authored by the reviewer or pushing unnecessary rewrites that serve the reviewer’s interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity on scope and applicability of guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that some recommendations are context/journal-specific and may not generalize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, follow the specific journal’s reviewer guidelines; otherwise apply broadly-applicable principles such as constructiveness and specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract should contain necessary components (Context, Objective, Methods, Results, Conclusion) and stand alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for discrepancies between abstract and full manuscript; ensure abstract provides concise summary highlighting key features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorship list should reflect individual contributions and an appropriate number of authors for the scope of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that authorship follows accepted credit norms and accurately reflects contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Title should accurately describe the study, be interesting, clear, concise, and relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the title draws the reader and reflects content without being misleading or incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Keywords should be appropriate and enhance discoverability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure keywords include the most appropriate terms for indexing and searchability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction should summarize what is known, provide rationale and goals, and identify a specific problem or knowledge gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for appropriate length, inclusion of recent relevant studies, and clear statement of study purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Background should describe the topic adequately and establish relevance of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that literature review and theoretical framing set the stage and justify the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature review coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Current and relevant work should be reviewed and key studies should not be omitted; paper should clarify its contribution relative to prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify omitted key references and assess how the manuscript relates to or contrasts with existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Study design should be appropriate for stated research objectives and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether choices (methods, imaging, analytic tools, statistics) are justified and whether design aligns with aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Results should be presented logically, balanced and unbiased, with results corresponding to each experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure data are appropriately measured and analyzed, and presentation follows the order of Methods where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion should be justified by results, put findings in perspective with prior literature, and note limitations and future research needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that conclusions are supported by data and that unexpected results and discrepancies with other studies are discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of fact should be supported by citations; avoid citing unpublished material inappropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify citations are correctly used and that claims are substantiated by accessible literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions should not overstate significance, generalize inappropriately, or engage in unsupported speculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that conclusions are valid, supported by data, and suggest realistic avenues for future research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference completeness and format
rubrics_metrics.description: All references cited in the text should appear in the reference list and vice versa; formatting should be correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for missing or extraneous references and correct citation formatting and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be clear, publishable quality, properly numbered, and include informative legends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether figures enhance understanding and whether any should be omitted or improved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should be properly labelled with correct units, self-explanatory without repeating text, and consistent with text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure tables summarize data effectively with clear headings and numbering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph accuracy and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphs should accurately reflect data with correctly labeled axes and appropriately displayed important results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check axes labels and variable representation for accuracy and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgments should mention funding agencies and roles, and recognize contributors not meeting authorship criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify funding disclosures and appropriate acknowledgment of contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary materials should be complete and included where necessary for transparency and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all related documents and supplementary data are provided and revised as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices should contain appropriate supplementary information, not material that belongs in the main manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest adding or moving content to appendices if it is appropriate supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research aim clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose of the paper should be clear and explicitly stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the research objective is clearly articulated in the Introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis clarity and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypotheses (if applicable) should be clear, testable, and relevant to the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether hypothesis indicates direction and clinical or theoretical relevance, and whether it has been previously investigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research question definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Research question should be clearly defined and novel or justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether the question is clearly stated and whether it has been posed before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem statement clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem being addressed should be clearly stated and justified as real and important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that the Introduction includes a concise problem statement that justifies the study’s contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory development quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Theoretical development should be strong, with rival theories considered and knowledge claims substantiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for appropriate theoretical grounding and avoidance of sweeping unsupported statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods transparency and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods should be well described, appropriate, and detailed enough to allow replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity of stepwise procedures, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and whether sufficient detail is provided for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data source reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Data should come from appropriate and reliable sources and be described with appropriate units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify dataset definition, appropriateness, and freedom from bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant description
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant or unit characteristics and selection criteria should be fully described when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check inclusion/exclusion criteria, population description, and appropriateness for the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment rationale and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each experiment should have a clear rationale and sufficient methodological detail; proper validation experiments should be performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure experiments are clearly justified, detailed, and validated appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on data-collection instruments (validity, reliability) should be provided and documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether instruments are described, provided if necessary, and referenced for unusual methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample collection and size justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples should be properly collected/processed/stored and sample size justified (e.g., power calculation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify sampling methods, sample representativeness, and whether power/sample-size calculations were performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study type identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should specify its study type (e.g., case report, cohort, review) and meet expectations for that type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm correct categorization and alignment with methodological and reporting norms for that study type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct — human subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies involving humans should state IRB approval and informed consent where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for explicit statements of ethical approval and documentation of consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct — animal subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal studies should demonstrate adherence to care/use guidelines and ethics review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify evidence of ethics review and compliance with animal welfare guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial or scientific conflicts of interest should be disclosed and considered when evaluating influence on research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether funding influenced access to data, authorship, or publication decisions and whether disclosures are complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundancy / plagiarism / self-plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript should not duplicate already published work or conceal relationships to prior publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for duplicate text/data, translation of published work without acknowledgment, recycled data, or copied figures/tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific contribution / value
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the paper makes a meaningful contribution to the field and whether that marginal contribution is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the manuscript is publishable in principle based on contribution relative to existing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / originality
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should be original, address something new, and not be a trivial extension of prior results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the problem, goal, or results are new or mere variations of existing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance / significance / importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess overall significance, importance, and interest of the results to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate scientific merit based on relevance to the field, statistical/clinical significance, and overall interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript should be concise, understandable, well-structured, and stylistically appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify sections to be reduced/expanded/added; evaluate paragraph structure, writing style, and logical flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar and language correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Grammar, syntax, spelling and word choice should be acceptable and not hinder comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for typographical and grammatical errors; determine whether language issues require a professional translator or copyediting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of abbreviations and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations, trade names, and symbols should be used consistently and terms sufficiently defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify inconsistent or unnecessary jargon and check that key terms are defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical flow and argumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should exhibit logical organization and smooth transitions across sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure arguments progress logically and that the manuscript allows evaluation of technical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall interest to readership
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the manuscript will be of interest to the journal’s readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check topical fit and likely interest across the journal audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit for the journal (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript content should be consistent with the mission and scope of the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify alignment with journal aims and scope before recommending publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the paper is concise or could be shortened to improve readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify redundancies and overly long sections that could be trimmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess for obvious biases created by procedures, presentation, or interpretation of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for unbalanced presentation, selection bias, or procedural choices that introduce bias.
